name: Aninda Roy Dhruba
intro: I study how learning systems can make better use of structure—and how their predictions can be evaluated beyond a single score. My work spans hierarchical medical classification, bias in NLP, and time-series forecasting.
about: I am a Computer Science and Engineering graduate of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET), and a Lecturer at Northern University Bangladesh. My research experience connects machine learning, optimization, and medical applications. I am preparing for doctoral research in Computer Science, with an interest in building medical AI systems whose objectives and evaluation reflect the structure of the problems they address.
direction: Building on my work in hierarchical classification and NLP bias, I hope to investigate how structured objectives, uncertainty-aware evaluation, and optimization can support more dependable medical AI. Reinforcement learning and intelligent control are further interests I would like to explore.

themes.title: Structure-aware medical AI
themes.text: Learning from patient dialogue while respecting relationships between medical specializations and diseases.
themes.question: How can training objectives preserve clinically meaningful consistency across prediction levels?

themes.title: Bias & model evaluation
themes.text: Understanding how bias arises and propagates through NLP training pipelines and decoding strategies.
themes.question: How can evaluation reveal failure patterns that aggregate performance measures overlook?

themes.title: Optimization & sequential learning
themes.text: Connecting experience in time-series modeling and ensemble tuning with an interest in reinforcement learning and intelligent control.
themes.question: How can optimization improve learning from temporal signals and inform future medical AI research?

research.title: Hierarchical medical dialogue classification
research.problem: Classifying patient conversations across 16 diseases and four medical specializations while maintaining consistency between the two levels.
research.contribution: Designed a hierarchical pipeline and custom multi-objective loss functions to jointly optimize inter-level consistency and classification accuracy. Fine-tuned BanglaBERT and ClinicalBERT and examined model complexity–performance trade-offs.
research.outcome: A portion of this thesis work was accepted at ICCIT 2025, as reported in the CV.
research.methods: Hierarchical learning / Transformer models / Loss function design

research.title: Bias propagation in NLP systems
research.problem: Understanding bias types and how their effects propagate across the NLP model development process.
research.contribution: Investigating 18 distinct bias types and propagation mechanisms across training pipelines and decoding strategies.
research.outcome: Survey paper published in Elsevier’s Array journal, as reported in the CV.
research.methods: NLP / Bias analysis / Training and decoding

research.title: Electrical load forecasting
research.problem: Forecasting electrical demand from historical Power Grid Company of Bangladesh (PGCB) load data.
research.contribution: Developed LSTM, ARIMA, and hybrid forecasting models. Applied signal decomposition, feature engineering, hyperparameter optimization, and ensemble tuning to capture seasonal demand patterns.
research.outcome: Reported 1.09% MAPE in the CV. Evaluation protocol and dataset period are not specified consistently in the source.
research.methods: Time-series analysis / LSTM / ARIMA / Ensemble optimization

projects.title: Diabetic retinopathy detection
projects.text: Combined five CNN architecture families—VGG, ResNet, InceptionV3, DenseNet, and EfficientNet—for multi-class retinal grading. Examined model agreement and uncertainty to guide ensemble weighting, with a Flask interface for inference.

projects.title: Competitive programming duel bot
projects.text: Built an adaptive challenge and skill-matching system using the Codeforces API and Elo-based rating updates. The project explores feedback-based opponent pairing; it is not presented as a trained reinforcement learning agent.

projects.text: Developed a service marketplace with bidding, user authentication, and real-time notifications, bringing together full-stack application design and data management.
